utterances.text: Looking at your diary, Exhibit P432, I will just mention the names of some individuals that you mention in your diary and then I will ask the question. So you named the following individuals: --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you link that to dates because the diary is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have the witness provided with his original, the Dutch copy of his diary, that may be of assistance to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I believe that would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe it's in the binder that has been provided to Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would refer to dates as well as to the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, I refer to the date of 11th of August, Friday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As you can see, Mr. Dijkstra, in the second paragraph in the English version that I have before me, there are names that are mentioned there are Olja and Sandra. Could you tell us, please, who are these people?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: They should be interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Two paragraphs lower, you mention the names Frank and Iva?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: Frank as a Belgian colleague. Iva as far as I remember, a Czech female colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the penultimate paragraph on the same page, and this is an entry for Saturday, 12th August, you mention the name Jurgen and Vesna?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: Sorry, my headphone went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not easy with one hand, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So in one before last paragraph, on the same page, Saturday, the 12th of August, the names Jurgen and Vesna are mentioned and it is said there that they intend to get married. Obviously, Jurgen is a person who is not local but Vesna, I assume is. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: Vesna is a Croatian is citizen and Jurgen is a friend and colleague of mine from old times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The 14th of August, the next page, Monday mention is made of a Duska?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: Duska was one of the few remaining is Serb interpreters that stayed with us after Oluja.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tuesday, the 15th of August, at the very end, the names Tudjica are mentioned, I think there is an error there, it's probably Djurdjica and Ljiljana, do you remember these people? You can is see this prior to the entry on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: If you want to know if I can remember the faces, no, I can't. I can remember that I had been talking to several people, and if I put the names with those dates, it should have been those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your diary, the entry for Sunday, the 20th of August, you mention again Duska and Iva, you've explained that but you also mentioned here that Alun Roberts for whom we know is the spokesman, the UN spokesman; and Iva prevented, forestalled an event. Can you tell us what kind of relationship they had?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: How do you mean that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know is if you put Iva and Alun Roberts in the same sentence, what kind of event was this. Can you recall the event?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I'm trying to wonder what the relevance of this line of question is and of this particular question. If we can just get some ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit, Mr. Mikulicic, that a similar thought came into my mind but then at the last question, I thought that's more about a specific event so to find out exactly with whom this witness had coffee, unless there's any specific reason to suspect that interpreters were spies or were having undue influence on decision-making, but of course just to go through the list of names of the ladies and then to find out whether they are Croatian or Serbian as such but of course I did let you go because I didn't know where it would end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just hope that here we have a specific event so please put that question but I would not encourage you to go through two months of coffee drinking and then to find out that 60 per cent was female, 40 per cent was male, et cetera. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the entry in your diary, the 21st of August, Monday, where you mentioned that you were writing a letter to a "Miss Anonymous," this was in parentheses ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have not yet dealt with the previous event, Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I thought we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you put a question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what I would like to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What kind of incident was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I think Mr. Hedaraly intervened and I just said that that was a specific event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: My mistake, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, that's 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let's get back to the incident where Alun Roberts and Iva prevent arresting at a checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember specifically that incident?

utterances.speaker: SWITBERTUS JOHANNES DIJKSTRA
utterances.text: I remember being told about that specific incident. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. [Interpretation] So let's go back to the entry for the 21st of August, Monday, where you are writing a letter to an attractive interpreter who you called "Miss anonymous." utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, the Chamber would like to deliver the reasons for a decision which was delivered already at an earlier stage. And these are the Chamber's reasons for granting trial-related protective measures for Witness 6. On the 20th of March, 2008, the Prosecution applied for the trial-related protective measures of pseudonym and face distortion for Witness 6. On the 2nd of April, 2008, the Prosecution filed a corrigendum to the application. The Markac Defence responded on the 1st of April this year and the Gotovina and Cermak Defence on the 3rd of April, 2008. All three requested that the Chamber deny the motion. On the 7th of April, 2008, the Chamber heard the witness on the matter of protective measures. At transcript pages 875 and 876, the Prosecution added a request for voice distortion, which prompted no change in the Defence's position. At transcript page 876, the Chamber granted the Prosecution's application for pseudonym, face and voice distortion, with reasons to follow. As the Chamber held in its reasons for its first protective measures decision in this case, which can be found at transcript page 2610 and 2611, the mere expression of fear by a person is not sufficient for protective measures to be granted. The party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. Witness 6, a Croatian Serb, has relatives who live and own property in Croatia, and he himself regularly returns to the country. In this case, the Chamber found that the expected testimony of Witness 6 could antagonize persons both in the areas where the witness's relatives live, as well as elsewhere in Croatia. Added to this, the witness is a relatively well-known figure and so easily identifiable. In the past, the witness had made public comments about various political matters and about the accused. While the Chamber was mindful of the Defence's argument that this could indicate that the witness did not in fact hold any fear for the security of his family, it noted that there is a difference between expressing an opinion in a public debate, and giving testimony in the context of a criminal trial. For the aforementioned reason, the Chamber finds that the Prosecution has demonstrated an objectively grounded risk to the security and welfare of Witness 6 should it become known that he has given evidence before this Tribunal. That is sufficient to warrant the granting of the requested protective measures which are of a nature to allow the public to understand the substance of the testimony. This concludes the Trial Chamber's reasons for granting protective measures for Witness 6. I'm looking at the Prosecution. I take it that there's no witness waiting out of this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact that -- and that's true for all the other documents we discussed a minute ago. The issue is not relevance. The issue is not reliability. That is the issue, not relevance, not reliability and as I said before, if apparently the Prosecution is not intending to ask permission to change its witness list; so therefore, it appears that they have no interest in tendering this evidence then, of course, it's for the Defence if it ever comes to a Defence case, if they want to have this in evidence to either present it under Rule 92 bis or present it under Rule 92 ter but as said before, the Chamber, and I think this has been discussed at various occasions and is at this moment, also not only the rules but I think also the practice of this Tribunal, if you want to change that, and if you want to -- if you want this Chamber to admit written statements outside the very specific rules 92 bis, 92 ter, 92 quater then you should make an application for us to revisit the issue. utterances.text: Then Mr. Kay, if there are full translations there and are they all uploaded into e-court.

utterances.text: Then all these documents, that is D347 up to and including 382 are admitted into evidence and, of course, we'll verify together with the registrar whether the -- all the translations are there. utterances.text: Then P23, the status of this number of reports changes from marked for identification into marked not admitted. Last one on my list is P320.

utterances.text: Then the Chamber will decide in due course on admission of P320 which therefore at this moment keeps the status of MFI.

utterances.text: Yes, that's what I take it that Mr. Kay understood and we understood well as well. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.
